utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We are to commence the Defence evidence, and we understand from yesterday, Mr. Djurdjic, the accused himself will now give evidence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. The first witness for the Defence is the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If the accused could come forward. Would you please take the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I shall speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What we have heard, Mr. Djordjevic, suggests that you could be in that witness box for well over a week. If you find that you are tiring significantly in that time, please indicate. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Djordjevic. Before we commence with the examination-in-chief, please introduce yourself to the Court and state your personal data.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I am Djordjevic, Vlastimir. I was born on the 17th of November, 1948, in the village of Kozica, Vladicin Han municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be so kind as to tell us what are you -- what is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I have a bachelor's degree in law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see exhibit D010582 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That is, Mr. Djordjevic, document number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask Your Honours, can we provide Mr. Djordjevic with a hard copy for his easier reference and for him to be able to more easily handle the document? Because it does not have any annotations or anything added subsequently, so it is quite clean. He can use it during the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be I think practical, Mr. Djurdjic, for you to provide the accused with hard copy documents when he's going to be making detailed reference to them, as long, of course, as they are not annotated in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, prior to today's session we received translations of all the documents that we are going to be seeing under a single number, except for one document, and I believe we handed over that one document to you this morning as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, please explain what this document which you have in front of you is.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision when I was admitted to work in the Ministry of the Interior, the secretariat of the interior, in Zajecar a month after graduation. So I was employed a month after graduation with the secretariat of internal affairs in Zajecar, and this precisely is the administrative decision stating that I was so employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 2 now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After having completed my apprenticeship within the secretariat in April 1973, I was assigned to the position of crime detective in the secretariat of the interior of Zajecar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This decision or by this decision I was assigned from my previous post to the post of inspector for white-collar crime or for the suppression of economic crime in the inter-municipal secretariat of the interior Zajecar. So it somewhat changed my status, and there was also a revamping within the secretariat. So instead of the secretariat of the interior of Zajecar, they set up the inter-municipal secretariat for internal affairs of Zajecar which encompassed several municipalities. And within such a joint inter-municipal secretariat, I was assigned to the post of inspector for economic crime. That was in May 1974.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 4 of this document which is in March 1995 -- 1975, the leadership of the then-inter-municipal SUP from the previous post of crime inspector for economic crimes, they assigned me to the post of inspector of the militia, police inspector, in the same secretariat so that as of the 1st of March, 1975, I was transferred to the uniformed segment of the force, and I was a police inspector within this inter-communal secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 5 now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In June 1976, from the post of police inspector I was assigned to the post of senior police inspector in the inter-municipal secretariat. A senior police inspector within the inter-municipal secretariat meant that I was the officer in charge of the uniformed segment of the inter-municipal secretariat, so I was the superior to all the police commanders of the police stations within the secretariat area, which there were eight at that time. I was responsible for the uniformed segment of the force in that regional, meaning for several municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see page 7.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, these are decisions -- or rather, this is a decision. Since there were certain reorganisational changes within the secretariat from the post of senior inspector I was assigned to the post of full inspector. Practically I did the same work. There was some revamping, there were some changes. So instead of the previous titles which I previously had, which was inspector -- police inspector or senior police inspector, they introduced the titles of full inspector, high inspector, high inspector first class, and -- so I was practically doing the same work but my status had changed in that respect because the regulations on the internal organisation and the job description scheduled within the inter-municipal secretariat had changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 8 now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Within that same secretariat there existed the post of assistant secretary for militia for police affairs, and I was assigned on the 1st of April, 1979, to that position while practically as assistant secretary for police affairs I was also the superior of all the police station commanders in the area. I answered to the head of that secretariat for the uniformed segment of the force and for their -- the discharge of their duties by them, by those officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page, please -- not in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision from late January, 1982, 29th of January, in fact. At that time it was assessed that I should be assigned to one of the positions within the republican secretariat of the interior. And so this is the relevant decision when from the inter-municipal secretariat of the interior in Zajecar I was transferred to work in the republican secretariat of the interior of the Republic of Serbia to the position of head of police department in the police administration of the republican secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the same decision. It had to do with my personal emoluments, my salary. That is why we saw it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision whereby -- from the -- my position I was promoted on the basis of my years of service and of my educational background. I was eligible for a higher post than one -- than the one that I was holding, so this is a decision that was brought so as to promote me to the post of senior inspector. So this is -- this was a decision on my promotion rank-wise within the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Since we can't follow this on e-court, could we just be given the dates of each individual page that he's referring to because that last one I'm not able to find so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Distinguished colleague, each document, there is the date on the top of each document. The date on which it was adopted and then by whom it was adopted. It is indicated. But you all -- you have received the hard copies of all these documents, I believe, haven't you? You can see 18th of May, 1982. It is written on the top of the document, if that is what you are referring to. Each document bears a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is what I was asking for, the date of the document that the witness is referring to. I didn't have it before. Now I know that we are speaking about a document dated the 18th of May. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, for easier reference, please always refer to the date. State the date of the decision that you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: So this decision is of the 18th of May, 1982, and it was adopted by the head of the administration for joint affairs within the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a decision of the 3rd of October, 1985. And as my previous post I had spent a required number of years. I was promoted to the position of senior inspector first class and the head of the administration for joint affairs brought this decision, promoting me to that particular position or to the rank of senior inspector first class.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision which was taken on the 27th of July, 1990, where the republican secretary assigned me from my position of head of police department where I had been working until that point to chief of the inspector for internal control of the legality of work in the republican secretariat, whilst holding the same rank according to the previous decision. So from the police administration I was transferred to be chief of the inspector for internal control of legality of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us just explain to the Court, it is stated here "republican secretary." According to the constitution valid at the time, was the secretary at that time what was later minister, corresponded later to the title of minister within the secretariat of internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That would in current conditions be a minister. At the time the designation was secretary, republican secretary, because the institution was the republican secretariat of the interior. At that time Radmilo Bogdanovic was the republican secretary. Later, instead of republican secretary, this became a ministry and hence all later senior officials were ministers, the heads of those institutions were ministers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Minister Zoran Sokolovic on the 31st of December, 1991, assigned me to the position of chief of police administration, my rank being the same one that I had at the time. So from chief of the inspectorate I was transferred, I was assigned, to the position of chief of police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see -- Your Honours, I move to tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00393.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Defence Exhibit D010-0582 -- no, we've already dealt with that. I beg your pardon. D010-0394.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 12th of September, 1996, the Government of the Republic of Serbia appointed me assistant minister of the interior at its session held in September 1996. The Ministry of the Interior was provided with a copy of this decision on my appointment as assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We notice, Mr. Djurdjic, that the name is not given of the witness. He is described only by position. Perhaps the witness could confirm that he was that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, technical mistake in e-court. So the next exhibit is the decision on the appointment. Here we only see that a decision on the appointment is enclosed, whereas in the next exhibit there is the actual decision on the appointment, however this is a technical error, and you will see from the next document -- or rather, the one that we're going to display. That's going to be that decision on the appointment. I would appreciate it if we could correct this, if the first page and this other page could be one single exhibit. I don't know whether that is possible at this point in time because this seems illogical the way we've entered it into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would seem that if they cannot be combined, the next document is the more important one. So we will see that on the screen at the moment, give it an exhibit number, and if the records officer is able to combine them, she will do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, could you please have a look at the document that is the second one under your number 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we see in e-court D010-0396.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, I see it. That's the decision that I'd like you to tell us about.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the government passed a decision appointing me assistant minister, and now the administration, the technical people within the government, are simply sending this on to the ministry. So this is the actual decision of the government appointing me assistant minister, and it is compulsory for this decision to be published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Serbia. It is dated the 11th of September, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be admitted as an exhibit together with the previous document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, those two documents will be Exhibit D00394.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a look at number 12, and that is Exhibit Number D010-0391.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision in which the Minister of the Interior, Vlajko Stojiljkovic, appoints me acting head of the RJB, the public security sector. Before that decision was taken, changes had been introduced, ranks had been introduced. According to the previous decision I got an appropriate rank, and it is in that way that he appointed me acting head of the RJB on the 30th of May, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D395.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Exhibit D010-0388.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision also taken by Minister Stojiljkovic. The date is the 27th of January, 1998. By this decision he appoints me head of the RJB, the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D396.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now see Exhibit D010-0599.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision that was passed by the Government of the Republic of Serbia on the 30th of January, 2001, whereby I was relieved of the duty of assistant minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be admitted into evidence -- I beg your pardon. I have just heard that there is no translation for this document, so then could it just be marked for identification before being admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D397, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have Exhibit D010-0399.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Djordjevic, could you please look at number 16.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. After having been relieved of duty - we saw the document a moment ago and then I ceased to be assistant minister - the then-Minister of the Interior, Dusan Mihajlovic, on the 31st of January, 2001, appointed me counsellor of the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D398.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have D010-0402.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that is page 17 for you, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is a definite decision for me. It was passed by the minister of the interior, and it states that my employment was terminated as of the 3rd of May, 2001, and that, even before I met the general pre-requisites for retirement, I was entitled to retire in accordance with Article 41 of the Law on the Interior, and the decision was passed on the 3rd of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that you would be pensioned off, or were you pensioned off and then informed -- or rather, were you informed of the termination of your employment?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when I was relieved of duties as assistant minister and when I was appointed counsellor to the minister, the minister decided that I should be a member of the coordination body for the south of Serbia. Practically from that moment onwards, that is to say from the 1st of February up until my retirement, I was a member of that coordination body in the south of Serbia. Practically, as the coordinating body we were responsible for the state of security in the three municipalities in the south of Serbia that border with Kosovo and Metohija. We also had other obligations in view of the land security zone, that is to say conditionally speaking that would be the administrative line facing Kosovo. Practically up until my retirement I was a member of that body and I was there. From time to time I did go to Belgrade. On that day, the 3rd of May, I finished the meeting that was chaired by Mr. Nebojsa Covic, who I think was deputy prime minister at that time, and he headed that coordinating body too. I think that the meeting was over by about 8.00 p.m., and then by telephone I was informed from Belgrade that I was being pensioned off and that I should go to Belgrade to receive this decision. On the very next day I went to Belgrade, and I received this decision on the 4th of January[as interpreted], 2001. I didn't know that I had been pensioned off. I didn't know anything about this. The first time I ever found out about it was in the evening of the 3rd of January [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this exhibit please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The translation has indicated the 3rd of January and the 4th of January. Should that be May? Lines 14.8 and 10 or 11.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the entire decision, the only date that is mentioned is the 3rd of May. There is no other date. It only says down here the 4th of May, and there is his signature, that is to say that the mentioned person received the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There may be a translation issue in the transcript, Mr. Djurdjic. It's a mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you please move on to document 18, if you need to have a look at it while giving your next answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I've forgotten to do so, I would like to ask that the previous exhibit be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The decision of the 3rd of May, 2001, will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D399.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, as for your entire career, you spent it in the Ministry of the Interior; right?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us a few words about who it is that is in charge of the Ministry of the Interior, and could you provide some basic information to us about the Ministry of the Interior as such.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: First of all, may I say that in the system of the state administration, it is the ministries that discharge duties that are of importance for the republic. So internal affairs is -- are taken care of by the Ministry of Internal Affairs, of the interior. Also the Law on State Administration, the Law on Internal Affairs, state that the minister of the interior is the head of the Ministry of the Interior, and from that point of view -- actually, first of all, may I say that the minister is elected or later relieved of duty by the Assembly of the Republic of Serbia. And in accordance with the laws that I have just referred to, the minister of the interior is accountable for the entire work and functioning of the Ministry of the Interior, that is to say that he is responsible -- or rather, he represents the ministry vis-à-vis all other state organs, and it is the minister's duty at the request of the government or the parliament or parliamentary bodies to provide information to the government or the parliament or parliamentary bodies about the work and the results of work of the ministry or individual issues that he's called upon to explain. In his capacity of minister, he was a member of the government as well, specifically in this particular case Mr. Stojiljkovic was also deputy prime minister; he was not only minister of the interior. But the Ministry of the Interior in all its domains - we'll probably deal with that a bit later - is headed by the minister of the interior in accordance with the powers vested in him by law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the minister submit reports about his work and the work of his ministry to some organs?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior through the minister, or rather, it is the minister who first submits an annual report on work to the Government of the Republic of Serbia and also to certain bodies in the Assembly or to the Assembly itself once he is asked to do so. So it was the minister's duty to submit a report once a year to the Government of the Republic of Serbia and permanently, at their request, to keep them informed about what the prime minister or the president of the Assembly are asking him to do. So he was the person who represented the ministry and who was duty-bound to inform the mentioned state organs about what had been done and how it had been done. Also as minister it was his duty to have direct co-operation with other state organs, other ministries, with the Army of Yugoslavia, and I don't know -- all those state institutions that are at that level where he is the representative of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me in what way the internal affairs are being carried out and who's the person who specifies that.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the laws that I mentioned herein above, the minister of the interior was authorised to issue other bylaws regulating the area of internal affairs, and in addition to that, also to issue internal enactments within the ministry itself. These internal enactments regulated within the ministry which jobs are going to be performed within the ministry, in what way, which organisational units are going to take care of them, et cetera. Practically by passing these internal enactments he regulated all the issues, he issued rules, orders, instructions, and other things. As for written documents are concerned, his role reflected in regulating all the issues by means of issuing books of rules, orders, and instructions. Those were the methods that the ministry as a state organ was duty-bound to perform, either through its organisational units or its various services.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to illustrate what you have just told us, can we please now look at Exhibit D101. That's number 19 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: A short while ago we saw the Law on the Internal Affairs, and in Article 7 of the said law it is stipulated that the minister is authorised to govern the way of conducting affairs within the ministry, and in accordance with this article the minister of the interior shall issue directions how the internal affairs are going to be conducted by people belonging to the reserve forces. This is only one of the directions that he was bound to issue, and he did issue a great many of them indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at Exhibit D101 -- I beg your pardon, 102.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's number 20 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. The previous direction that we have seen, so to speak, is a kind of general enactment stipulating the engagement of reserve forces, and the next document that is, so to speak, of a lower-ranking status stipulates how this previous direction is going to be implemented in practice, precisely and specifically how these reserve forces are going to be -- how to carry out certain peacetime [indiscernible] for the ministry by the reserve forces, it was issued pursuant to Article 28 of the Law of the Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia. And this order governs the issues of serving summons, engaging reserve forces by quoting which rights and obligations such persons have once they are summoned pursuant to this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this order I see that the period from the 1st of July until 31st of December, 1998, is mentioned with regard to the engagement of reserve forces. Can you tell me, is it possible to engage people from the reserve forces without an order of this kind coming from the minister?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: As I said, this is an order which provides for operationalisation of the previous direction. So twice a year the minister would issue this kind of order that would remain valid for the following six months. Pursuant to this order and only in this way could he engage any member of the reserve forces in order for them to carry out certain peacetime tasks within the Ministry of the Interior. In this manner, practically throughout the whole year, throughout the whole 12 months, there was an order in force issued by the minister of the interior which practically sanctions and approves the use of the reserve force and envisages what their obligations are. In addition to that, the order provides for the relevant administrations in the ministry and the secretariats that are obliged to ensure that this order is going to be implemented as stipulated in the order itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, could you remind us of the date of Exhibit D101, the document preceding this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document D101 is dated 22nd of June, 1998. 22nd of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And D102 is the 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please previously turn to 21 now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document on screen is D102, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and the witness -- or rather, the accused already spoke about it. Now I would like him to tell us just briefly something about the document 103, what's the difference, and to what period it pertains.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This previous order was in force from the 1st January 1990 -- from the 1st July 1998 until the 31st of December, 1998. In order to avoid any gaps on the 31st of December the minister issued the next order that was going to remain in place for the next six months containing the same obligations that I already spoke about. Therefore, there was always the minister's order in force which enabled the engagement of the reserve force for the purpose of their carrying out certain peacetime tasks in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, these orders and directions all refer to the engagement of the reserve forces in peacetime. In wartime can you tell us what the procedure was with regard to the reserve force under the Law on the Interior?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: The same procedure. The minister has to take a decision in order to engage the reserve forces following the mobilisation and in accordance with the wartime plans of the ministry. Thereby, the reserve forces were attached to the Ministry of the Interior which were already prepared by the Ministry of the Interior. And this reserve force can only be engaged by virtue of a decision issued by the minister. There was no other way for that to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the Ministry of the Interior in case of war has its own war units, reserve war units?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Starting from the municipal organ of the interior, which is the lowest organisational unit within a secretariat. In a municipality there is a war unit of the police and it went all the way up to the secretariat of this specific municipality. All the municipalities had those wartime police units made up of members of the reserve force generally in the ratio 1:1, which means there was one member of the reserve and one active-duty police officer. The reserve force also was engaged in the so-called special police units, but pursuant to their war plans the Ministry of the Interior already had wartime police units prepared in combination with the active-duty force in the ratio 1:1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was the status of the reserve police officers when they become engaged?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: By virtue of the direction and orders issued by the minister, the status of these members of the reserve forces is decided and defined whether they be engaged in peacetime or in wartime. In other words, once they are admitted into the reserve force and once they become engaged, from day one of their engagement a member of the reserve force of the police or the Ministry of the Interior acquires a status of an authorised official, and he is entitled to all other rights affordable to any other authorised official. That is to say, when it comes to active-duty police officers he exercises the same powers of an authorised official as they do and he also has other entitlements arising from the employment just like any other active-duty policeman, that is to say he is entitled to a salary, he is entitled to daily allowances, he has a right to a sick leave or the right to receive medical treatment if injured while carrying out duties. This is equal to every other -- to what every other active-duty police officer enjoyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, let us now move to the questions relating to the internal organisation of the MUP and the closest associates of the minister under the rules of internal organisation. First tell me who adopts these rules? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: As we already mentioned, in accordance with the Law on the Internal Affair, the minister of the interior is the one who adopts the rules of internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior. And in principle, these rules on the internal organisation in its first segment encompasses all the duties and jobs that specific organisational units of the ministry are going to discharge, and this is described in the Law on the Internal Affair. This same enactment says that the units which are attached to the headquarters of the ministry, what they're going to do, also detached units that are in the secretariats, and other units. The rules on internal organisation contains all the duties and responsibilities of all these organisational units, whether in the headquarters of the secretariat, the ministry, and other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me this, these rules passed by the minister, does this have to receive an approval by the government?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The minister prepares a draft of the rules, and this draft is then offered for adoption by the Government of the Republic of Serbia, who give their approval. The moment they give their approval it practically become to be enforced in compliance to what the minister had proposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the period while you were head of the public security department, were there any assistants in the ministry and what were their duties and who appointed them, although you already said that based on your personal experience?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, the Government of the Republic of Serbia at the proposal of the minister of the interior appoints assistant ministers in the Ministry of the Interior. So the government is the one who makes these personnel decisions, and after that, the minister is bound to issue decisions in -- and issue instructions and assign certain domains to every assistant. At the time when Minister Stojiljkovic was in this position --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at Exhibit P263.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's number 23 in your binder, sir.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is a letter from the minister of the interior dated the 4th of June, 1997, in which he informs the organisational units of the public security department at the MUP headquarters all the secretariats, all the centres of the state security department, the MUP staff in Pristina, border police stations, the police academy, the post-secondary school of internal affairs, the secondary school of internal affairs, and the institute for security. So, as I've already said, at this point in time in the public security sector four assistant ministers were appointed by the government decision. That was Radomir Markovic, Stojan Misic, Obrad Stevanovic, and General Petar Zekovic. I was assistant minister from 1996 onwards, as we've already seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you. I'm sorry. In paragraph 2 could you please have a look who it was that was appointed at the session of the 4th of June.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you explain that to us.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A bit earlier the government had appointed assistant ministers, namely myself, Stojan Misic, and Radomir Markovic, and on the 4th of June Major-General Petar Zekovic and Major-General Obrad Stevanovic were appointed. So in this dispatch the minister of the interior, through the powers vested in him by law, is making his assistant ministers in charge of particular fields. So Radomir Markovic is in charge of crime police affairs -- police work actually, then analysis and information; Major-General Stojan Misic is in charge of matters related to foreigners, administrative and legal affairs, fire prevention, police and communications affairs; Major-General Obrad Stevanovic for affairs relating to the police administration and the operations centre, also for the secondary school and the college of internal affairs and the police academy; whereas Major-General Petar Zekovic is in charge of affairs related to the administration for joint affairs and the boarder and lodging administration. At that point in time the minister, by his decision, appointed me head of the public security department -- acting head, actually. As is stated in this dispatch, the assistant ministers helped the minister in carrying out duties pertaining to the province of work of the administrations that they were in charge of. So Radomir Markovic made certain proposals to the minister in order to improve on the work of the crime police and everything that is related to that. And that had to do with crime throughout the territory of the Republic of Serbia. So at every point in time the assistant ministers also were supposed to transmit the orders of the ministers -- the minister to people in the field, in the areas in which they were responsible. So on the one hand they were making proposals to the minister, and in this way they were helping him carry out his duties as minister; and then on the other hand, they were conveying the minister's orders, requests, et cetera, down the line in that field of work in which they were responsible for helping him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There is one thing that I find striking here. All the lines of work that are mentioned here, that the minister is in charge of and that his assistant ministers are in charge of, all of this has to do with public security?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Practically for every line of work, for every administration and headquarters, the minister charged every one of his assistant ministers who would be keeping him abreast of what was going on in that particular administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you were assistant minister and chief of the RJB.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Acting chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Acting chief.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: At that moment and through this instruction that was given by the minister or this information and the assistant ministers had these narrower responsibilities for the functioning of particular sections within the RJB in the secretariat headquarters. In some way he diminished the role at that point in time of the acting chief of the RJB, because instead of -- instead of the heads of administrations being directly responsible to the head of the department and then the head of the department to the minister - as was customary in the system in terms of superiority, et cetera - the minister on the basis of the rights vested in him by the law, he made assistant ministers in charge of particular tasks. Perhaps it was easier for him in that way to have more direct links to the administrations. But at any rate, through this mode of organisation of work in some way the role of -- the role of the assistant minister who was in charge of the RJB was diminished, and that was I at that point in time. So the situation was not fully clear as for immediate responsibility, and as for relationship of hierarchy, of who is the superior and who is below that superior, as is customary in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, all the assistant ministers are equal and they cannot issue orders to one another; right?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I as assistant minister --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw the question. I withdraw the question. I do beg your pardon. I do beg your pardon. I'm obviously still cross-examining. May I re-formulate? Oh, no, I won't. Let's just move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, you may not. In the top echelons of the MUP was there another method of work in the form of a collegium?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. In the Ministry of the Interior and earlier on while there was still a republican secretariat of the interior, there was always a collegium of the minister and also the -- there was a collegium of the chief of the RJB. As for the collegium of the minister, in this period, that is to say from the beginning of June 1997 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Up until that period, tell us what was it like while the minister was Sokolovic, while it was Sokolovic who was the minister.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I've already said that the institution of the collegium as a method of work and leadership in the ministry existed before Vlajko Stojiljkovic came as minister -- became minister. So Minister Zoran Sokolovic had his collegium consisting of the heads of the RJB and the RDB. I think there was also an assistant for joint affairs, for finance, et cetera, but basically it was the minister who had a collegium that consisted of the chiefs of services, that is to say of the RJB and the SDB. As for public security, I was a member of the collegium of the chief of the RJB because at that time I was head of the police administration. Once a week we had collegium meetings of the head of the RJB, and every one of us reported on his own line of work in terms of what had been done during the previous week. And then there would be a proposed plan of work for the following week. At that collegium of the chief of the RJB, decisions were made practically on all matters and that is where decisions were made how and in which way certain tasks would be carried out. If there were any controversial matters, of course it was the chief of the RJB who would make the ultimate decision. If there were any controversial matters, then he would communicate with the minister, he would clarify the matters involved with the minister, and he would convey to us what the position was as agreed upon with the minister in practical terms. When Minister Stojiljkovic became minister, I as acting chief of the RJB and later on in 1998 when I became chief of the RJB, I never held a single collegium of my own, that is to say there was no collegium of the public security. The minister of the interior once a week invited to his collegium all the heads of different lines of work in the headquarters of the ministry, that is to say all the heads of administrations, then he'd call the chief of the secretariat of the -- of internal affairs in Belgrade and all the assistant ministers in the ministry. At this collegium the minister -- or rather, at first I would open the collegium and I would give the floor practically to the chiefs of administrations in public security. The chiefs of administration would report on the situation in the preceding week, and also they would say whether there were any proposals for the following week. Then assistant ministers would take part in the discussion. Every one of them made their own contribution as they deemed fit. I also, if I had anything to observe, I could say whatever I wished to say and then the minister would conclude the collegium in the following way. He would issue orders as to what would be done in what way, who would cooperate with who in carrying out these tasks and who would perhaps even be involved from outside the ministry, and so on. After the heads of administrations would report, then in the conclusions the minister would give guide-lines, detailed guide-lines, to all the administrations in the public security sector. Whatever the minister would say at that point in time had to be carried out as he had said because within a week's time he would ask for information, for feedback, as to what had been done in the meantime. That is the way in which this collegium operated. This was supposed to be the collegium of the public security, but it wasn't really because the collegium was chaired by the minister, and he issued tasks there too. So in a way it was the collegium of the minister rather than the collegium of public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After such a collegium would any conclusions be written up?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the collegium most often it was the head of the analysis department, and he would take the minutes. After the meeting it was his duty to send the conclusions to all assistant ministers and heads of administration, that is to say all the participants in the meeting. It was his duty to send the conclusions and all the instructions provided by the minister in writing, and it was on the basis of that that everyone operated during the following week.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, please, could we have Exhibit D208.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You have that under number 24.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision of the minister on the 4th of -- dated the 4th of December, 1998. In this decision he establishes in formal terms his own collegium. In the meantime - I just have to say one more thing - there were certain personnel problems -- or rather, there were certain solutions that were worked out in the state security sector. Instead of Jovica Stanisic, assistant Minister Radomir Markovic was appointed head of the SDB and Nikola Curcic, Major-General Nikola Curcic was appointed as his deputy. So Radomir Markovic until then, who was in charge of crime and analysis, and now he became head of the SDB. Through this decision, the minister sets up his own collegium consisting of the head of the RJB, the head of the SDB, and his deputy. Assistant Ministers Obrad Stevanovic, Stojan Misic, and Petar Zekovic and also, Lieutenant-General Dragisa Dinic who was head of the administration for traffic police and also he was assistant chief of the RJB. On the next page we see the Major-General Dragan Ilic chief of the crime police administration was also included and appointed as member of the collegium and also Major-General Branko Djuric, chief of the secretariat of the interior in Belgrade. What is also envisaged here is that collegium meetings should be attended by the chef de cabinet to the minister and Slobodan Krstic, head of the analytics department, who was in charge of keeping the minutes. Also, the possibility is provided for other senior personnel from the ministry to attend collegium meetings on the basis of a special decision made by the minister. That is what is written in this decision. In actual fact, these meetings that were held once a week were always attended by all heads of administrations in the RJB, just like before and in the same way reports were made like before and conclusions were drawn up the same way like before. If I can put it this way, the only new thing here is that the collegium meetings are attended by the chief of the SDB and his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that in practice heads of administration who participated from the public security sector. Did heads of administration from the state security sector also attend these meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: No, this collegium meeting was never attended by heads of administration of the state security department. The chief of the department and his assistant were there, and as a rule the chief of the department would inform the minister on a couple of matters which he considered should be made available to the minister and that is where his briefing ended. As far as the leadership and senior officials from the public security department is concerned, everything remained the same as prior to the adoption of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, after these collegium meetings did you hold also collegium meetings of the head of the public security department?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: After this collegium, I never held any meetings because all the senior officials, all the line of work senior officials and the assistant ministers who were responsible for the specific segments of work in the ministry would present all security parameters, all the problems that they were confronted with, as well as all the proposals that they had for work in the coming period. All of that would be reflected in the conclusions of the minister, who would then instruct everybody how to go about finishing their particular segment of the work. So I, just as all the other assistants and heads of administrations, only had to implement the work assigned to me within the next days and ensure the overall functioning and the execution of the work falling within the competence of the ministry, both on the ground and in the particular secretariats. So I did not have my own collegium meeting as the chief of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe it is time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, you described how it was until the 4th of December and you told us something about the 4th of December as well. I would like to know, though, whether the minister up until the 4th of December, 1998, had his own collegium meetings that would be attended by the chiefs of both departments and the assistants.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. It's possible that at some point in time we did meet with the minister in that composition, but that wasn't his style of work really. He would call the chief of public security when he needed him, when he needed chief of state security he would call him, when he need any other assistant ministers in terms of their line of work he would call them individually, that is to say that the collegium of the minister never met, as is written here in this decision, which is to say with these nine men, with General Branko Djuric, Slobodan Krstic, and Pantovic. This collegium never met with the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But would you please carefully listen to my questions. I asked you about the situation up until the 4th of December, 1998, was there -- were there any collegium meetings that would be attended by both the chiefs of the RJB and state security? Who was the chief of state security at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I think up until October or November it was Jovica Stanisic, who was the chief of state security, and at that time there never was any collegium meetings with the minister that would be attended by the chiefs of both the RDB and RJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You as assistant minister, could you issue tasks to another assistant minister and vice versa?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: As I have told you earlier, this type of organisation in a way disturbed the relationship that existed between the administrations within the ministry and the chief of the RJB. As for me personally, I was assistant minister and my relationship with other four assistant ministers from the public security was such that I could not issue any orders to them. That means that all orders, instructions, tasks, and so on could only be issued to them by the minister himself. I could not issue any orders or tasks to my peers, to other assistant ministers. That means that all assistant ministers were responsible to the minister directly. They were responsible to him for the task that had been issued to them by him. A bit earlier we spoke about how Radomir Markovic transferred and became chief of state security - if I'm not mistaken - sometime in October of 1998. Yes. Earlier on we saw in a dispatch that he was responsible for crime investigations, police administration, and also for the administration for analysis and information. When the minister appointed him chief of the RDB, he decided that the administration for analysis and information need to be linked in via General Stojan Misic to the administrations for which General Misic was responsible to the minister. And he was tasked with coordinating the work of the administration for analysis and information. At that point the minister said that his further communication with the chief of the crime investigations police administration would be direct. So that means that there was direct relationship between them, and he, the chief of that administration, was directly responsible to the minister, that is to say that none of the assistant ministers were any longer in charge of the crime investigations department.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to put the most important question to you concerning the security and -- or rather, I would like to tell you that the most important question in Yugoslavia at that time concerned the security and political situation in Kosovo. So what were the topics discussed at these collegiums held by the minister?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: At these collegiums in the form that they were in, we received -- rather, the minister was informed in most general terms about the situation and the problems if the RDB had some observations they were provided but also in global terms. The chief of the department would inform on that. And as for other lines of work within the ministry, and none of them briefed about the tasks and jobs conducted down there in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. The police administration, in fact, informed the minister only about sending certain individuals, police members, down there and also about equipment and weapons and also members of joint services who provided logistical support to these units, to PJPs, also informed the minister. But there was no special information given about anti-terrorist activities in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. This wasn't the topic at any of the meetings, not at all. All that was given was just general information, something that was widely known to everybody. There was no detailed information provided about anti-terrorist and combat activities conducted in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have a document before you, it has two pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 3, please. I think it was D209 -- I apologise, 208, not 209.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In this exhibit we have page 3 and we will get to it. Now, tell me, please, based on what you know, was this page a part of the document that we saw?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: This is the first time I see it -- or rather, I saw it during our proofing, but in my view this is a document that the cabinet of the minister prepared so that he would have a list of the participants. This is not an official document on the composition of the collegium; this is simply a list of persons that are already mentioned in the decision. This is not a part of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know who drafted this?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, you see that this is a list of collegium participants and ten people are listed, and then below that we have a list for RDB. Can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about this. All of these persons were mentioned earlier in the minister's decision on establishing the collegium. Now, why they were divided in this list, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Members of the collegium are listed in the decision, Danilo Pantovic, head of the office of the minister; and Krstic Slobodan, chief of the IT administration only attend collegiums according to the decision but they're not members of it.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and this is why I think that somebody else drafted this list based on the people who attended collegium meetings, but what their criterion was I don't know. Pantovic and Krstic were not members of the collegium. In the basic decision they are not listed as members of the collegiums. This is probably just an auxiliary document that was prepared for the minister so that he could see who participated in those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, this was drafted according to the same principle, collegium in its expanded composition, which includes chiefs of administrations. In addition to Pantovic and Krstic, here, just for the record, they also included other participants of the collegium. There are two names here that are questionable in my view, Momo Stojanovic and Zavisic. I don't know who drafted this and what criteria they used to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know whether this would be a good time, but I have to comment on the last two pages of this document. Not knowing that there was already an OTP exhibit that had been used here, we also obtained from the national council an official document on the collegium of the ministry without these two enclosures, attachments. And I think that these two attachments are not authentic, that they're not original attachments to the decision that was admitted into evidence. I think that this was produced by somebody subsequently, not at the time when this document was adopted on the 4th of December. And we think so especially in view of the way that the names of the persons are listed on pages 3 and 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Djurdjic, that's an interesting question. We have the document with the pages attached. We have this witness expressing a view that it may not be as he understood it. It will be a matter for other evidence, if there is any, or for a decision by the Chamber in due course. At the moment it's an open question. I just want you to be aware that because you think it is something else, that doesn't mean that it's necessarily so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Just for the sake of clarification, the exhibit which we received by official channels, is it in that form that we should tender it before the Court, because the numbers here indicate that we used an OTP document, K054-1171, that's one page; and the other page is K054-1171. When we received these documents officially, we didn't get that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The first document's number is K054-1172.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us move on, Mr. Djordjevic. Did the minister of the interior appoint the chiefs of the secretariats of the interior in the territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In accordance with his legal powers, the minister decided first on the admission of all staff to work at the Ministry of the Interior, and later also about any promotions, personnel promotions, personnel assignments throughout the service. To that effect, the minister also made decisions as to whom he would appoint to the position of chief of administration at the headquarters of the ministry or chief of a secretariat, namely, these most responsible positions within the secretariat. And he would adopt relevant decision assigning them to such posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have Exhibit D010-0600. According to the 65 ter list, it is 1787.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Djordjevic, you please take a look at serial number 25.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision by which on the 4th of June, 1997, the minister appointed Branko Djuric as chief of the secretariat of the internal affairs in Belgrade, and prior to that he held the position of chief of department of internal affairs at Novi Belgrade. But as of that point in time the minister appointed him under this decision to the position of chief of secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I can see on this decision that the date when it was brought was the 4th of June, 1997.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, you were appointed as acting head of the public security department on the 1st of June, 1996. So I would like to know whether the minister consulted you in respect of the appointing of this most important position, that of chief of secretariat of the interior in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: As according to the job description schedule, I was the senior official in charge, at least I was the acting head in the public security department. It would have been normal for me keeping with the powers pertaining to that post to have been asked about the appointment of staff to the most important positions, in particular in respect of chiefs of secretariats. As the chief of the public security department, I had a right to propose certain appointments to the minister - and I'm referring to the most important once again, namely, chiefs of administrations or chiefs of secretariats. This is the normal order of things, the normal course of things. However, the minister, without consulting me in any way whatsoever, brought this decision appointing Branko Djuric as chief of secretariat so that I only heard later by word of mouth or in the news that he had been appointed chief of SUP, of the S-U-P, which was totally out of the customary way things were done because at that time I was the acting chief of the public security department. But it is the way it was. So that after all he has the legal authority, he has the possibility to do so, whether he would see fit to consult someone or not was up to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask for this exhibit to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D400.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please tell us with regard to the period of your work as chief of the security department, were there any other cases of decisions having been taken by the minister without any consultations whatsoever with you?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Of course there were such instances. There were a number of such instances. There were different appointments that had been made in respect of which he made his own decisions without consulting at all or obtaining the sense, the opinion, of, for instance, the chief of the public security department. This could have referred to specific security duties and jobs which the ministry carried out or the internal organisation, so to speak, of work within the ministry. A typical example, for instance, was that at the end of 1998 he decided in agreement with the state security department to have the special unit from Novi Sad dismantled and for a part of the men to be assigned to the state security department, i.e., to their special operations unit and that the commander of that unit according to his decision was assigned to the post of deputy commander of the special operations unit. It would have been quite regular for him to have consulted me somewhat in that respect, but he did not. I learned about that from the commander of the unit, Branko Curcic, that is the special unit from the Novi Sad who came to see me. And he told me that he had been called by people from the state security department and that according to instructions from the minister they had decided to take over most of the members of that unit into this special operations unit and that he personally was to be assigned to the position of deputy commander of the special operations unit. And he asked me what was he to do, and what else could I tell him but simply I just told him, "You have no other option, you have no choice, just accept what you are being offered," and that was the way it was done. Then the minister called me and he told me that a part of the unit was to be transferred into the state security department special operations unit and that the other members of the unit, which that unit would not wish to take its into ranks, would have to be assigned to the territorial unit of the secretariat for internal affairs of Novi Sad. I issued orders to the secretariat's head to that effect, so to in fact take in these actually surplus members from that unit who we assess could go there. We also took part of the members into the Belgrade department. So this was the way in which this unit from Novi Sad was dismantled, in the way that I have just described. There also had been other security relevant situations, just as the appointment of Djuric, for instance, there was the relieving of office of some heads of -- in the service without me knowing anything about it. He would send, for instance, an assistant minister to dismiss some chief in the service, and to me he would just say, "Now find a position for this person, for so and so, and see where you can put him." This was as far as personnel was concerned, as far as staff was concerned. As regards to the actual work depending on his assessment and his own choices, he would assign some people to be in charge of certain work without taking account in so doing of some standard, hierarchical relationships in the service. A characteristic example is the assistance that was rendered on one occasion in connection with a Studio B independent television station, which being independent in its way was actually -- bore the brunt of the current authorities. And at that time the decision, a judicial decision in fact, was taken for that TV studio to be extinguished. He issued instructions to that effect. Members of the police in SUP Belgrade, the police brigade of the SUP Belgrade were engaged to carry out that task. This assistance was rendered and the staff of the TV Studio B were expelled. And in accordance with the judicial decisions, that matter was dealt with in that way. So that was a very important question which he decided on himself -- organised himself through various superior officials. I only learned about it the next morning when I came to work, that that had been done the previous night. The senior officials who had been ordered to do that came to me and told me that that had been done, and they told him -- me that one of his requests when he charged them with this task was that they should not tell me about it. Now, why he did so, I really don't know. I have some explanations in my mind, but I really do not actually know. On that occasion either I -- neither on that occasion did I go to see him and seek any explanations; I was just simply informed that this had been done. So -- and as the police was -- and that the police a part of their public security department had been engaged, not only had he not informed me, but he had in fact forbidden the people who had done this job to inform me of it in any way whatsoever and there had been other instances as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have Exhibit D38.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is your number 26.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is a decision -- a decision by which the minister actually assigns Dusan Gavranic from the position of chief of the secretariat of the interior in Zrenjanin to the position -- assigns him to the position of chief of secretariat of the interior in Gnjilane. On that occasion he tasked me, the minister, that is, with calling the chief from Gavranic and communicating to him the minister's decision which was that he was to be assigned to the secretary in Gnjilane. I think -- in fact, I do not think, I'm sure because I was aware what the situation was like, that Dusan Gavranic actually fell out of favour with the minister because he did not do something he wanted him to do in connection with some structures in Zrenjanin. And he thought that when I communicated to him the minister's decision, that he would be appointed to Gnjilane, that he would refuse that, and that thereby his service, his employment, with SUP would be terminated. However, I called Gavranic, he came to see me, and I told him that there existed the need because the Gnjilane chief was to be retired and there existed the need for another chief to be appointed to that position. I explained to him in a couple of sentences that many of our people and many of our senior officials were going down there to work. And he only asked me, "When am I supposed to go?" And I informed the minister accordingly, this decision was taken accordingly, he went down there, and I believe that he did his job successfully. So that it was decided in that way, and thus by the minister and he assigned Gavranic as chief of the SUP in Gnjilane and that was his decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have Exhibit P78, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Your number 27.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision of the 15th of April, 1999, under which Lieutenant-Colonel Vucina Janicijevic is appointed to the position of chief of the secretariat of the interior in Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Who brought this decision?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Also the minister, and the decision was served on Janicijevic on the 22nd of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't hear you, when was it adopted?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I did say it was on the 15th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have Exhibit P77.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decision dated the 15th of April, 1999, as well. I passed this decision as the chief of the department and in accordance with the powers vested in me by the minister. In this decision Colonel Ljubinko Cvetic, an employee of the Ministry of the Interior in the Kragujevac secretariat shall cease to perform the tasks and duties of the chief of the Kosovska Mitrovica secretariat of the interior, where he was sent on the 1st of January, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The decision on appointment was made by the minister, and then on his order you had this person reassigned to the same SUP?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that's not the only such case --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I didn't object on a couple of occasions to leading questions of this nature, but sometimes I get the translation a long time after the question has been asked and answered. I think counsel should be careful --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you object?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I object because it's leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm just asking for an explanation, an explanation of the appointment. It's the 15th of April, 1999, and a new chief of the SUP was being appointed, and it's signed by the minister. And then according to the authority given to him by the minister, the chief of the RJB gives a decision on the cessation of duties of the hitherto chief of SUP. I want him to explain the situation, the witness to explain the situation. What is leading in that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour, basically he tells the witness that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No need, Mr. Stamp. You're telling the witness really what you think the answer to your problem is instead of inviting him to tell you; that's the basic problem. It takes away the reliance we can place upon the answer given by the witness; that's the disadvantage from your point of view. So I think over this particular issue the ground has been lost, it's too late.
